title: Activation habit book and ops procedures
content:
Purpose:
This working notebook collects the day-to-day rituals, signal taxonomy, and lightweight decision heuristics for gradual exposure of LLM-driven features. It is intended to be pragmatic — a small set of repeatable actions that cross-functional teams (product, engineering, SRE, data science, support) can adopt when we ship staged experiments, canaries, or A/B tests that touch inference routing, model changes, or cost/latency tradeoffs.

Design principles (short):
- Make activation a habit: reduce cognitive load by standardizing pre-flight and in-flight checks.
- Signal-first decisions: prioritize actionable signals over long lists of metrics.
- Human-in-the-loop, automated-first: automate obvious rollbacks, keep humans for judgment calls.
- SLO-aligned: align exposure decisions to customer-facing SLOs (latency, error, quality).

Stakeholders and roles (one-liners):
- Release steward (owner): orchestrates the activation window, runs preflight checklist, primary comms channel.
- Oncall SRE: watches infra signals, can trigger emergency cut if platform degradation observed.
- Model owner / ML Eng: monitors quality regressions and model-specific telemetry.
- Product PM: validates the experiment hypothesis and tracks business metrics.
- Support liaison: surfaces early customer issues and triages user-facing regressions.

Signal taxonomy (keep it small — 6 buckets):
1) Platform health (required): total requests, p95 latency, error rate (5xx), per-region saturation.
2) Cost & throughput: tokens/sec, GPU utilization, average tokens per request (for batching).
3) Behavioral quality: intent drift, hallucination rate (annotated sample), rerank score delta.
4) Safety signals: safety classifier triggers, escalations to moderation queue.
5) Business impact: funnel conversion delta, retention proxy (7d active), top-level KPI wiggles.
6) Sampling checks: manual review samples, human-labeled failure rate for random cohort.

Primary thresholds (examples — adjust per-product baseline):
- Platform: p95 latency increase > 20% over baseline AND p95 > 500ms -> immediate investigation; if sustained 15m, consider rollback.
- Errors: 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase or doubling over baseline -> automatic traffic pause.
- GPU saturation: host CPU/GPU throttling events > 5% of nodes -> activate reduced exposure.
- Model quality: annotated failure rate > 8% on safety/accuracy tests -> pause model rollout.
- Business: conversion uplift must meet min detectable effect within 48–72h window; otherwise keep control.

Preflight checklist (to be completed by steward, in order):
- Confirm hypothesis and success criteria with PM.
- Create experiment ticket and link to monitoring dashboards (include sampling dashboard).
- Register traffic slices and identify golden cohorts and exclusion lists.
- Validate SLOs and alerting runbooks are wired to the steward channel.
- Prepare safety whitelist and human review cadence (if applicable).
- Smoke test on staging with synthetic traffic (latency, token accounting).
- Create rollback artifact (route toggle, model pin, cache clear plan).

Activation choreography (first 6 hours cadence):
- T=0: activate 1% traffic slice; steward announces start, links dashboards and sample viewer.
- T=10m: steward sanity check (platform + basic quality); if OK, move to 5%.
- T=30m: run automated sample capture and quick annotation (10 examples). If sample issues, hold.
- T=90m: if signals stable, ramp to 20% for more robust signal.
- T=3–6h: evaluate business KPI delta and medium-term stability; decide ramp to full or maintain as experiment.

Communication templates (steward channel post at each step):
- Start: "Activation START — feature: <short> | steward: <name> | slice: 1% | dash: <link> | smoke: ok?"
- Ramp: "Ramp -> 5% at T+10m | p95: 260ms (+3%) | errors: 0.03% | sample: 0/10 fails"
- Pause/rollback: "ROLLBACK: reason: <metric> | action: toggled route -> control | time: hh:mm | next: postmortem"

Automated guards (recommended lightweight automations):
- Auto-pause rule triggered when 5xx > threshold OR p95 > threshold for 10m.
- Traffic cap enforcement: maximum allowed ramp step per 30m window unless steward overrides.
- Sample flagging: pipeline that surfaces flagged responses to human annotators in the steward queue.

Escalation ladder (short):
1) Steward (first line) — immediate routing changes.
2) Oncall SRE (platform degradation).
3) Eng L3 (serving/runtime) for kernel/compilation/sequence-length issues.
4) Exec on-call (major customer impact or compliance issue).

Mini postmortem template (fill within 48h):
- Title / shorthand feature name
- Dates and windows of exposure
- What happened (timeline, signals observed)
- Root cause hypothesis (platform / model / data / traffic)
- Actions taken (rollback, patches)
- Next steps (monitoring changes, preflight updates, owners)

Sampling protocols (practical):
- Always capture 1% random sample of responses across slices for first 72 hours.
- Push 100 labeled examples to the steward queue at T+24h for quality audit.
- If safety flags appear, escalate to human review immediately and quarantine affected cohorts.

Retrospective notes (living):
- Keep the first two ramps short (<= 2 hours) to surface obvious platform regressions without large user-facing exposure.
- We under-index on human review in most rollouts. Plan annotation slack in roadmaps.
- Automations should default to safe (pause), but require a steward override path to continue when noisy metrics are expected.

Open questions / decisions for follow-up:
- Define a company-wide baseline cadence for steward check-ins (daily vs hourly for long experiments).
- Decide minimal sample size and labeling SLA for behavioral checks.
- Ownership matrix for long-running A/Bs: steward rotation frequency and reporting.

Quick links and artifacts: JIRA-ENG-3421 (ramp automation), https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Signal+Lexicon, github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts/pull/78

Notes to self (shorthand):
- Try a "steward-buddy" practice where two people share duty for the first 24h to avoid gatekeeping errors.
- Prototype a single dashboard tile that shows: p95 change, 5xx delta, annotated failure rate, business KPI delta.

If you own the next activation, copy this doc, fill the preflight checklist, and tag the following in slack: #rollouts, @oncall-sre, @models.
